summary.headline: Neapolitan Codices 22–24
summary.text: Descriptions of Neapolitan codices 22–24: a fifteenth-century manuscript with excerpts from John Laurentius Lydus on months, a Claudius Tuscus calendar, Zoroaster’s oracles with Pletho’s exposition, and Pletho on fate; a 1558 codex with prolegomena to Ptolemy’s Almagest, an astrolabe treatise, eclipse calculation, logistics, the Almagest, and Adrastus’s harmonic works; and a fourteenth- or early fifteenth-century codex with Ptolemy’s astrological works and an anonymous exegesis on the Tetrabiblos.
